stream: Armament — firing feel, ripple broadside, weapon archetypes
goal: Firing stops being a passive DPS stream and becomes a committed act. The player presses one thing and their battery ripples fore-to-aft down the engaged flank over 0.33–1.25 s, one gun at a time, the hull shouldering away as the wave travels. The length and shape of that wave is a live readout of state the game already simulates and has never shown during a fight: a hole in the wave is a dead barrel, a late beat is a worn feed, a gun firing into empty space is a frozen traverse ring, a wave that stops two guns early is a mount that cooked or ran dry. Routing power to weapons compresses the wave audibly; starving it stretches it. Three verbs total — salvo, side-select, charge-and-release — and no new ship state. HOWEVER: recon says the spec cannot be built as written. Two of its four named defects are still real, one is stale, one is real but its proposed fix does not work, and two further blockers were found that are worse than any of the four: the recoil model is physically inert against PlaneBody's velocity servo (measured: exactly 0.000 m of displacement), and the geometry and the simulation disagree about which side of the ship is port. The ripple is a feature about which flank is firing; it must not start until that is settled.

steps.change: PREREQUISITE, NOT MY FILE — DECISION FIRST. Resolve the port/starboard handedness contradiction. Facts: CRUISER_ANCHORS.port = [-158,46,60] and starboard = [158,46,-110] (hardpoints.js:132-135), i.e. port geometry is at -X; every NPC hull agrees (coalition.js:1130 fg_port mount [-48,5,12]; coalition.js:1125 subsystem 'stbd_battery' at [40,6,12]). But the port hardpoint is authored yawCentre: +PI/2 (hardpoints.js:209), and the sim resolves a bearing as worldForward.set(sin(heading+yawCentre+traverse),0,cos(...)) (ship.js:141-142) with yawOf = atan2(x,z) (physics.js:35-36) — so +PI/2 points at +X. The port battery's firing arc therefore covers the STARBOARD beam. selftest.mjs:203 bakes this in ('desiredHeading = atan2(1200,1200) - PI*0.5 // open the port battery'). ARCHITECTURE.md contradicts itself: line 109 says starboard is +X, line 115 says port is +PI/2; under three.js's right-handed frame with forward +Z and up +Y an object's right is -X, so line 115 is correct and line 109 — which the geometry stream followed — is the error. Either flip six anchors plus ~26 yawCentre values in art/geometry/ships/**, or mirror every module's authored X. Nothing exposes this today because _fire spawns from mount.worldPosition (correct side) and aims at the target, and mount.worldForward has exactly one consumer (vfx/weapons.js:431, the spark spatter).
steps.why: The entire headline feature is 'which flank ripples'. A ripple that runs down the port sponson while the recoil shoulders the ship the other way, on guns whose arc is on the far side, is not shippable. This is cheap to fix now and enormously expensive after per-emitter flashes and directional recoil exist.

steps.change: PREREQUISITE, NOT MY FILE (Ship & refit). refit.js:215-216 double-mirrors the starboard mount: `mirrored = hpId === 'starboard' && def.hardpoint === 'port'`, then `localPosition = new Vector3(anchor[0] * (mirrored ? -1 : 1), ...)` and `yawCentre = -hpDef.yawCentre`, where `anchor`/`hpDef` come from the TARGET hardpoint, which is already on the correct side. A port-authored module fitted to starboard therefore simulates at x = -158 (the port side) with yawCentre +PI/2 (the port arc), while its geometry is mirrored to +X. Both flanks become the same flank. Negate only when the AUTHORED side differs from the target side AND the anchor being used is the authored side's.

steps.change: NEW. Export RIPPLE {step .110, stepMin .070, stepMax .240, cadenceExp .5, mountGap .090, jitter .018, sweepMax 1.250, deadPause .055, frozenPause .140}, SALVO {lockout .35, heatMul 1.15, radiatorSurcharge .18, surchargeTime 3.0}, CHARGE {time 2.60, timeMin 1.20, timeMax 6.00, abortRefund .60, holdMax 4.00, ventHeat .25, dmgFloor .35, accFloor .55}. One SalvoController per ship: arm(side,{immediate}) / fire(plan) / fixedUpdate(dt) / get active. SLOT POOL: preallocate MAX_SLOTS = 24 slot objects at construction ({mount, emitterIndex, localZ, localX, time, action}); arm() fills a prefix and sets _n. Nothing allocates per salvo. ARM: walk ship.weapons; skip def.type==='pd' (locked AUTO), fireMode!=='SALVO', excluded mounts, !usable, stall>0, cooldown>0, stores.blockedReason(mount); filter to the requested flank by mount.hardpoint; if !immediate also require mount.canBear at arm time. emitterCount = clamp(moduleDef.muzzles?.length ?? 1, 1, min(8, def.shotsPerBurst)); mirror x for a port-authored module on starboard. ORDER: sort by ship-local emitter z DESCENDING (mount.localPosition.z + muzzle.z, unmirrored), tie-break |x| descending, then declaration index; sort in place with a module-level comparator. SCHEDULE: t=0; for each slot, if slot.mount !== prev then t += mountGap; slot.time = t + rng.signed()*jitter; t += stepFor(slot); if t > sweepMax rescale every step by sweepMax/t clamping each to stepMin and re-walk. stepFor: cadence = max(0.05, powerFactor * fireRateMul(mount.condition) * mount.parts.fireRateMul) — the identical expression at combat.js:150 — then step = clamp(RIPPLE.step / cadence**cadenceExp, stepMin, stepMax); DEAD slots return deadPause, FROZEN slots return step + frozenPause. NOTE the spec double-counts mount.parts.fireRateMul: §1.3 puts it inside cadence and §1.4 applies it AGAIN as step × min(1/mul, stutterMax). Keep it in cadence only — that reproduces the spec's own §1.3 table (dead feed 0.35 → 186 ms), whereas the §1.4 rule gives 264 ms, past stepMax. RELEASE in fixedUpdate: while slots[_i].time <= _t, re-test mount.canBear AT slot.time (this one line is the entire fire-early mechanic), roll misfeed once at each mount's first slot, stores.consumeShot, call combat._fire(ship, mount, lead, target, powerFactor, emitter), then drop all remaining slots of that mount if it tripped / jammed / ran dry. A slot that cannot fire is NEVER removed — it occupies deadPause or frozenPause. On exhaustion set each participating mount.cooldown = def.cooldown / cadence and emit EV.SALVO_COMPLETE {fired, dropped, reasons}. RNG: this.rng = world.rng.fork(`salvo:${ship.id}`). SCRATCH HAZARD: _updateShipWeapons uses scratch.v1 for the lead and _fire uses scratch.v3 (combat.js:137,236); recompute the lead into scratch.v1 immediately before each _fire and hold no scratch vector across the call.
steps.why: This is the feature. Deriving the step from the cadence expression that already exists is what makes the wave a live readout of power routing, condition and feed health without one new state variable — which is the design's whole claim to depth under scope-decision.md's four-question test.

steps.change: Two lines. ShipThermal.onShot (heat.js:218-224) gains a third argument `salvo = false` and multiplies th.perShot by SALVO.heatMul (1.15). ShipThermal gains surchargeTimer; update() (heat.js:152-212) multiplies this.radiate by (1 - SALVO.radiatorSurcharge) while it runs, decrementing by dt. Arithmetic checks out against real constants: Heavy Broadside heatPerShot = HEAT_PER_SHOT.cannon 0.030 × clamp(340/45, 0.4, 2.2) = 0.030 × 2.2 = 0.066 (heat.js:59-79); at balanced power 0.066 × 1.10 × 1.15 = 0.0835/shot = 0.334 per 4-gun salvo, against a shed of 0.085 × (0.4+0.65) = 0.0893/s over a 5.0 s cooldown. Net negative — sustainable. At assault power 0.110/shot = 0.440/salvo against a 2.5 s cooldown — net positive, the fourth broadside cooks the battery.
steps.why: This is the alpha-versus-sustain decision, and it falls out of two constants because heat.js already models radiate/load coupling. A thermal trip already sets online=false, offlineReason='heat', burstRemaining=0 (heat.js:227-246) and already costs 16 hardpoint structure and 0.02 condition, so the salvo controller only has to drop that mount's remaining slots.

steps.change: CROSS-STREAM (Physics). RECOIL = {bank 0.012 rad/shot scaled by damage/300, bankDecay 2.2/s, bankCap 0.075 rad, rise 14/s}. PlaneBody gains recoilBank and recoilRate; integrate() advances recoilBank by recoilRate*dt then decays both toward zero at bankDecay and clamps to bankCap; applyTo (physics.js:153-156) becomes object3D.rotation.set(0, this.heading, this.bank + this.recoilBank, 'YXZ'). DO NOT ADD ANYTHING TO body.velocity. firing-feel.md §5.2's lateral shove is inert: PlaneBody.integrate is a velocity SERVO, not a force integrator — physics.js:131-134 computes diff = target - velocity where target = forward × maxSpeed × throttle × engineEfficiency, clamps diff to maxDv = accel × engineEfficiency × dt, and adds it. With accel 14 (game.js:310) maxDv = 0.2333 m/s per step while the per-shot impulse is 0.045 × 340/300 = 0.051 m/s, so |diff| < maxDv, the clamp never bites, and velocity is set EXACTLY to a pure-forward target. The lateral component is deleted before the 0.55/s bleed at physics.js:140 ever sees it. Measured headless at rest, half throttle and flank: peak |vx| = 0.000e+0 m/s, net lateral displacement = 0.000 m. Even with the servo removed, a 4-gun Heavy Broadside salvo peaks at 0.174 m/s and displaces the hull 0.366 m total — at CAMERA.defaultDistance 3200 m and fov 46 (units.js:60,65) that is about 0.15 px at 1080p. The ONLY term that can read is the roll: 0.012 × 1.133 = 0.0136 rad/shot, and with bankDecay 2.2/s over 110 ms steps the four shots accumulate to 0.0136 × (1 + 0.785 + 0.616 + 0.484) = 0.039 rad = 2.25°, not the 3.1° §5.2 claims (the spec forgot its own decay). For scale the existing cosmetic turn bank reaches 0.13 rad = 7.4° (physics.js:121), so 2.25° is ~30% of a hard turn — visible, and in the right channel. ORDERING REQUIREMENT: apply recoil from the salvo controller at order 40, before the ships system at order 60 (game.js:185-190). Because nothing touches body.velocity, _updatePropellant (stores.js:268-300, which bills against measured velocity change) sees nothing and bills nothing — firing-feel.md §5.2's 'Required, or the numbers lie' _prevVel advance is unnecessary and should be deleted from the spec. If any future change does push velocity, it must run before order 60 or it is billed twice.
steps.why: Answering the parent's question directly: the recoil couples to PlaneBody through the cosmetic bank channel and through nothing else. The specified translational coupling is provably zero, and even the idealised version is sub-pixel.

steps.change: NEW headless proof tool, modelled on src/sim/selftest.mjs (which passes 51/51 today and needs no GPU — makeWorld at selftest.mjs:55 builds a World against a fake renderer). Twelve measurements, each exiting non-zero on failure. See the `verification` field for the exact list.

A ripple asserted by a screenshot is a ripple nobody can regression-test.

verification: node tools/ripple.mjs   — the proof tool. Twelve assertions, exit non-zero on any. (1) ORDER: record (t, hardpoint, emitterIndex, shipLocalZ) for every released slot; assert shipLocalZ is monotonically non-increasing and t strictly non-decreasing across the released sequence; print the wave as a table a human can read. (2) CADENCE: every inter-slot gap within [stepMin - jitter, stepMax + jitter]; a same-mount gap carries no mountGap and a cross-mount gap does; total sweep <= sweepMax unless stepMin*(n-1) exceeds it. (3) POWER READS OUT IN THE RHYTHM: same hull, same seed, three presets; assert sweep(assault) < sweep(balanced) < sweep(run) and print the three against the spec's 234/330/660 ms for a 4-gun bank. This is the check that proves the ripple is a live readout and not an animation. (4) HOLES: destroy a mount's 'output' sub-part (parts.get('barrels'), damagePart until destroyed -> parts.inert); assert the SLOT COUNT IS UNCHANGED, that no EV.WEAPON_FIRED came from that mount, and that the gap is deadPause +/- jitter. Asserting the count is unchanged is what stops a future refactor silently removing dead slots, which firing-feel.md §1.4 says would destroy the mechanic. (5) STUTTER: destroy the 'feed' part (parts.fireRateMul -> 0.35 via PART_EFFECT.feedFireRate); assert that mount's steps grow by 1/0.35^0.5 = 1.69x and the sweep still completes. (6) FROZEN: destroy the 'traverse' part; assert the slot still fires, its step is step + frozenPause, and with the target outside frozenAt +/- PART_EFFECT.traverseFrozenArc (0.07 rad) the round and the heat are spent and no damage lands. (7) DIES HALFWAY: force a misfeed (condition 0.3, seeded) and separately force a mid-sweep thermal trip; assert every remaining slot on that mount is dropped and no slot on any other mount is. (8) RAN DRY: mount.ready = 2 against a 4-emitter mount; assert exactly 2 fire and cooldown >= 0.5. (9) DETERMINISM: run the same salvo twice from the same seed; assert the released (t, mount, emitter) tuple sequence is identical. (10) NO ALLOCATION: assert SalvoController._slots.length never changes after construction and arm() returns the same object identity; heapUsed growth over 500 salvos under --expose-gc below a few KB. (11) EMITTER INVARIANT (the §8.3 regression test): for every registered module with a weapon, assert muzzles.length === weapon.shotsPerBurst AND that the count is identical at lod 0, 1 and 2 — this is exactly the check that would have caught firing-feel.md §1.1's table being wrong. (12) AUTHORING INVARIANT (the §8.2 regression test): for every module with ammoClass !== null, assert readyMax >= shotsPerBurst. Fails today on dorsal_missile_cells; that is the point. The tool must drive combat.fixedUpdate/ship.fixedUpdate directly rather than through Engine.frame, because SIM.maxSubsteps = 6 (units.js:92) and loop.js:143 resets the accumulator on saturation, so at 4x on a slow frame a sweep can lose steps and the tool would be measuring the loop instead of the ripple.

Adopting `turnExp: 1.35` would cost 13 points at half speed, i.e. it would do the opposite of what its own paragraph argues for, because that paragraph is argued against exp 1.0 and the code's baseline is exp 2.0.

Measured turn-authority delta: -0.7% at 25% throttle, -3.0% at 50%, -8.6% at 75%, -26.3% at flank. `src/sim/ai/shipAI.js:98-103` stations capitals at throttle 0.26–0.40 and line 442 clamps to 0.10 while coming about, so the working band barely moves — but this must be confirmed against the broadside-bearing probe, not asserted. For contrast, adopting the spec's exp 1.35 would cost NPCs 7.5% / 15.1% / 21.4% / 26.3% across the same band, which is why I am not proposing it.

**A constant angAccel cannot be global.** `controls.md:1063` declares 0.030 rad/s^2 flat. Applied to PlaneBody unconditionally it gives `coalition_corvette` (turnRate 0.58) a 19 s yaw spool and `coalition_strikecraft` (2.4 rad/s) an 80 s one — every escort in the game would stop being able to turn. It must be an optional per-class field with `?? maxRate * 2.4` preserved as the default. This is the single easiest way to break the game while 'implementing the spec'.

**Adding accelRetro without touching stoppingTime() silently breaks every move order.** `PlaneBody.stoppingTime()` (physics.js:96) divides by `this.accel`; `MoveController.update` (line 286) budgets its brake point from it. With retro 5.5 against accel 8.0 the controller under-predicts by 45% and the ship overshoots markers by ~557 m at cruise, then re-targets and S-curves back. Nothing in the tree would catch this — smoke passes, selftest passes.

**Adding accelRetro without setting it during transit invalidates the whole travel layer.** `src/world/travel.js:438-440` and 458-459 state, correctly today, that throttle-zero decelerates at exactly the acceleration rate, and `legProfile` (78-91) is a closed form built on that symmetry. Asymmetric retro makes every published leg time (151 / 225 / 312 s and the SILENT 217 / 330 / 497) wrong, and with them the propellant quotes and the interception percentages the player agrees to at plot time. The fix is three lines in `_enterTransit`/`_exitTransit` and it is easy to miss.

**The spec's slow turn is one leg of a three-legged system and the other two legs do not exist.** `controls.md:1136-1142` says the 12.5x turn-radius spread is what makes `Z` hard burn 'worth a whole power channel and a 40 s cooldown' and makes `R` reverse 'genuinely useful'. `Z` is bound to salvage (controls.js:278) and there is no reverse order or event. Landing §6.1's magnitudes without those two is adopting the punishment without either escape valve — strictly worse than what ships today. If a future stream implements hard burn and reverse, revisit turnRateAtRest downward; until then 0.165 is the honest number.

**Raising mass 62,000 -> 620,000 makes ramming viable.** The player goes from absorbing 61.3% of an overlap with a Bulwark to 13.6%, and from 27.1% to 3.6% against an Ardent frigate. Check whether `onImpact` (physics.js:343) feeds a damage model scaled by closing speed alone or by mass; if the former, a 620,000 t hull becomes a free weapon against anything it can catch. This is a real gameplay consequence of a change that looks like a units fix.

**The refit recalibration cuts the propellant penalty from 6.57x to 1.28x** at the max fit, via `src/sim/stores.js:285`. That is almost certainly the right call — 6.57x means one reversal costs 46 of a 640-unit tank — but it is a deliberate softening of a scarcity mechanic that `scope-decision.md` says must bite. If propellant needs to stay punishing, give it its own exponent rather than reusing massLoad linearly.

**The 6.2 deg heading overshoot is intended and will still feel wrong to somebody.** It is what `controls.md:1093-1096` asks for and the current code produces exactly 0.00 deg, so this is a visible behaviour change on every order. At 1000 m from a wreck (salvage beam range is 1800 m, `RANGE.salvageBeam`) 6.2 deg is ~108 m of lateral drift before it settles. `angAccel` is the knob: 0.055 gives 10.0 deg, 0.070 gives 6.2 deg, 0.090 gives 3.7 deg, and the 180-deg time barely moves across that range (20.0 / 20.2 / 20.0 s). Tune it in play, not on paper.

**acceptance.md:64 changes its numbers even though it cannot regress.** The criterion is a lower bound ('cannot change heading instantly') and 20.2 s > 15.2 s, and 'degrades with the square of speed' stays true because turnExp stays 2.0. steps.change: NEW, ~130 lines, no game code. This is the proposed measurement for the one blocker HANDOFF.md:108 records as 'not measurable; still open'. WHY surface.mjs CANNOT SEE IT: it measures the MAGNITUDE of the luminance gradient, and a smooth 200 m mound and a staircase of eight flat plates can carry the same mean |dL|. What separates them is whether that gradient is spread evenly over every texel (a mound) or concentrated into a few texels with flat ground between them (plates) — a statement about the DISTRIBUTION, not the mean. On a crop of ONE continuous lit face, per scanline, after a 5-tap MEDIAN (not a box blur — the grade's film grain is impulse noise and a box blur smears it into every neighbour, which zeroed the ramp detector on the first run), report: GRADIENT GINI (concentration of |dL|; 0 = a mound, 1 = a hard edge), PLATEAU COVERAGE (share of the face inside flat runs >= 8 px), PLATEAUS/100 px, STEP CONTRAST (mean |dL| between adjacent plateau means), RAMP FRACTION (share inside a monotone-within-tolerance run >= 40 px). MEASURED TODAY on the committed before/after pair, same crop: `close-before.png` gini 0.756, plateau coverage 36.5%, step contrast 0.0401; `close.png` gini 0.855, coverage 66.3%, step 0.0817; `docs/probes/cruiser.png` flank gini 0.869, coverage 45.9%, step 0.1018. The metric moves monotonically in the industrial direction across the known art commits, which is the validation it needed. MAKE GINI THE HEADLINE NUMBER: Gini is invariant under multiplying every gradient by a constant, so an exposure change cancels exactly — which is precisely what look-target.md:12-16 demands of any art-style measurement. Step contrast and ramp fraction are exposure-dependent (ramp went 6.4 -> 37.1 across a pair whose p95 also went 0.455 -> 0.702) and must be normalised by the crop's own p05-p95 range before they are quoted. Ship it with NO pass band until it has been run on the same six references ship-language.md:781-791 lists, exactly as §3 established 62/21/14; an unanchored threshold here would be invented, and this project has been burned by invented thresholds.
steps.why: 'Pillowy, not industrial' is the last of the blind critic's four blockers still open, and it is open precisely because nobody wrote a number for it.
